title: The Insider Question
question: Which behaviour can be established without turning a policy observation into a claim about motive?
briefing: A manager reports an employee’s unusual export; a colleague says it was approved. These reports conflict. Neither report establishes the person’s intent. Your authority is to acquire records and recommend a session-scoped response through Information Governance. You cannot approve your own control or disable an entire account or service.
lesson: Intent describes a purpose; a source recording an action usually cannot establish that purpose.

entities.name: Named export-workspace session
entities.impact: The workspace supports legitimate reporting. Findings must distinguish the observed session action, the approval boundary and any separate people process.
entities.capability: Named session and disclosed source paths only; no account-wide or host-wide control.
entities.dependency: The workspace supports legitimate reporting. Findings must distinguish the observed session action, the approval boundary and any separate people process.

entities.name: REVIEW-10 context
entities.purpose: Related context that must be assessed separately
entities.impact: Do not generalise the primary session finding to this separate scope.
entities.capability: Only the explicitly delivered relationship and source records.
entities.dependency: A separate task or observation does not supply approval for the primary session.

mechanic.question: Which behaviour can be established without turning a policy observation into a claim about motive?

options.label: Report the observed behaviour and approval boundary; leave motive unresolved
Infer malicious intent from a policy exception
Adopt the manager’s report as the verdict

limits.label: A policy or approval mismatch does not prove malicious intent or identify the human operator.
Unavailable collection does not establish that no activity occurred.
The source identifies a session or credential, not a person or motive.
Other scopes and their remaining questions need their own evidence.

queries.label: Establish the task and business consequence
queries.question: What is this service for, and which consequences change investigation priority?
queries.can: Names the normal task, related scopes, owners and interruption consequence.
queries.cannot: Does not establish who performed the current action.

queries.label: Check the exact work authorisation
queries.question: Does approved work cover this session, task, target and period?
queries.cannot: Does not prove the human operator or the activity that actually occurred.

queries.label: Inspect the scoped session activity
queries.question: Which action was recorded for this named session within collection limits?
queries.can: Records session-level actions and the observed target.
queries.cannot: Cannot identify a person, establish motive or reconstruct missing historical collection.

queries.label: Check the service transaction independently
queries.question: Does the service-side transaction establish the same scoped operation?
queries.can: Tests the operation through a separately collected service transaction.
queries.cannot: A second card alone does not establish a sufficient explanation.

facts.title: Starting observations
facts.text: A manager reports an employee’s unusual export; a colleague says it was approved. These reports conflict. Neither report establishes the person’s intent.

facts.title: Task, scope and business consequence
facts.text: Aggregate reporting is routine. Row-level customer exports require a named exception and approved destination. Investigation may document actions and approval scope; motive requires separate evidence.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The exception register explicitly approves this session’s row-level export to the designated internal review destination for this period.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The session’s export matches the exception register’s dataset, destination and period. The conflicting reports can be reconciled for this scoped action.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The receiving-system ledger independently confirms the approved review destination and dataset for the named session.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The exception register explicitly approves this session’s row-level export to the designated internal review destination for this period. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The exception register contains no approval for this session’s row-level export to the destination used. That absence bounds authorisation; it does not establish a malicious motive.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The session exported customer rows to a destination outside the approved exception. The activity is a policy/scope observation, not proof of an employee’s motive.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The receiving-system ledger independently records the row-level delivery outside the approved review destination and ties it to the named session.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The exception register contains no approval for this session’s row-level export to the destination used. That absence bounds authorisation; it does not establish a malicious motive. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: Work record unavailable
facts.text: The work-authorisation archive is unavailable for the named session and period. No approval or denial can be inferred.

facts.title: Session collection unavailable
facts.text: The session-audit source did not collect the relevant historical interval. Absence of a record cannot establish the absence of activity.

facts.title: Independent collection is limited
facts.text: The independent service journal lacks the target application operation for the historical interval. A different source name does not restore that capability.

facts.title: Verified check timed out
facts.text: The pre-established directory contact did not respond by the stated due step. This is a delivered limitation, not approval or a reason to wait indefinitely.

facts.title: A later scoped transaction
facts.text: The named session performed a further source-recorded operation within the specifically approved task. This later event does not identify the person, establish motive or change any earlier snapshot.

response.control: Restrict only the named organisation-controlled session

glossary.definition: Intent describes a purpose; a source recording an action usually cannot establish that purpose.
The target, operation and interval a source is capable of observing.
The explicitly named session or service covered by a claim and next action.

reviewWindow: The named session from its start through the explicit cutoff of each acquired snapshot. A simulation step is an investigation opportunity, not a minute.
